lesson.title: Seis, Siete, Ocho, Nueve, Diez: A Counting Song with Big Moves
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Sol remembers counting all the way to cinco — but today the count keeps going, all the way to ten! Get ready for big body movements with every number.
Stomp your foot and say [[seis]] — that means 'six'! Reach both arms way up high and say [[siete]] — 'seven'! Spin around once and say [[ocho]] — 'eight'! Echo Sol slowly: seis... siete... ocho...
Touch your toes and say [[nueve]] — 'nine'! Now jump up with your arms in the air and shout [[diez]] — 'ten'! Sing it fast now: ¡seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez!
You counted all the way to diez with big movements — seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez! Tomorrow, get ready to toss beanbags and count every throw.

objectives: Count aloud from seis to diez (six to ten), producing each new number word with its own body movement
Perform the extended count-to-ten song alongside a caregiver at both a slow and a fast tempo
materialsNeeded: Sol the puppet (or stuffed animal/toy from previous weeks)
Open floor space for big body movements — no other materials needed
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Gather with Sol and review counting uno through cinco with fingers, then tell your child today's song keeps going all the way to diez with big body moves.
2. Stomp a foot and say seis together; reach both arms up high and say siete; spin around once and say ocho — pause after each for the echo.
3. Touch your toes and say nueve; jump up with arms overhead and shout diez, until your child has performed all five new movements.
4. Sing the whole extended song fast, adding a big move for every number: '¡Uno, dos, tres, cuatro, cinco, seis, siete, ocho, nueve, diez!'
5. Repeat the slow-then-fast pattern 2-3 more times, letting your child choose their own movement for each number.
6. Close by asking: 'Can you count all the way to diez with me, using your favorite big move?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: keep the movements to seis, siete, and ocho for the first few rounds, adding nueve and diez once those feel automatic
Ready for more: after counting up to diez, try counting back down to seis, reversing each movement
This is a speaking-and-movement activity — your child never needs to see these numbers written down to learn them
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken counting-and-movement activity — success looks like your child attempting the new movement for each number seis through diez out loud, not a written right/wrong answer.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Opens week 4's ACTFL Presentational Speaking target (WA-WL-2015.1.3) — counting aloud to ten — by extending week 3's finger-counting song with a full-body movement for each new number, shifting the child from recognizing numbers by ear toward confidently producing them aloud for an audience, exactly the oral/aural-first approach this K-2 band calls for.
